newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity follows cash, COB down, PV up.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity follows cash, COB down, PV up.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures followed physical prices Tuesday with California Oregon Border (COB) finishing lower while Palo Verde (PV) ended higher, industry sources said.

Physical prices in the Northwest were reported to have fallen today on surplus power supplies, while prices in the Southwest were said to be lower due in part to a short-term coal plant outage in the Rocky Mountains.
Power futures were said to have followed suit, with little other fundamentals to move the market, the sources said.
October California Oregon Border ended down six cents at $16.16 per megawatt hour after trade in a range of $16.05-16.60, while November finished down 15 cents at $16.45 per megawatt hour.
Remaining COB deferreds finished down between five and 20 cents.
October PV ended up five cents at $16.65 after trade in a range of $16.60-16.80, while November closed also up five cents at $15.45.
NYMEX said an estimated 136 COB and 35 PV contracts traded Tuesday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
